questions.question: Transduction is the
options: conversion of physical energy into neural firing.
response of our sense organs to stimulation.
interpretation by the brain of a sensation.
cessation of response of sense organ due to prolonged stimulation.
questions.reference_answer:
「轉換作用」（transduction）是感覺系統的核心步驟，將外界物理能量轉換成神經系統可以處理的電訊號。

轉換作用就像神經系統的翻譯官，把世界的語言（光、聲、壓力）翻譯成大腦能理解的訊號。

options: by the pattern of neural activity of many olfactory receptors.
by specific receptors responding to specific odors.
according to the place on the olfactory epithelium which is maximally stimulated.
by the olfactory bulbs.

嗅覺的運作原理與組合編碼（combinatorial coding）

組合編碼（combinatorial coding）機制：每種氣味會活化一群嗅覺受器，大腦根據這些放電的整體神經圖樣來判斷氣味。這種方式用「少量元件」達到「大量組合」。

questions.question:
When you see your professor in the supermarket, you have trouble recognizing her. What best
explains this?
options: The relations between geons are contrary to your expectations.
A familiar stimulus in an unfamiliar context is difficult to recognize.
You have used bottom-up processing instead of top-down processing.
Ambiguous stimuli are easiest to judge in familiar surroundings.
questions.reference_answer:
知覺中的上下文效應（context effect），以及熟悉刺激在不熟悉情境下的辨識困難

× Context Effect（上下文效應）： • 我們在熟悉情境下，會啟動相應的知覺預期 （top-down activation） • 熟悉刺激若出現在不熟悉情境，會讓我們錯過或誤認它（如穿便服的警察、素顏的老師） ×Top-Down vs Bottom-Up Processing : • Top-down：先有預期與經驗，再理解當前刺激（大多數人臉辨識依賴 此 • Bottom-up：完全依賴感官輸入逐步建構理解

The pattern of sleep cycles varies with age.
The sleeper gradually moves from wakefulness to deep sleep after the first two hours of sleep.
all of the above are true

questions.question: Chris has a painful knee injury and takes medication. After several days, he needs two tablets for the same effect.
options: addicted to the drug.
becoming psychologically dependent on the drug.
developing a tolerance for the drug.
showing withdrawal symptoms from the drug.
questions.reference_answer:
藥物對神經系統影響的基本概念：耐受性（tolerance）、依賴（dependence）、成癮（addiction）與戒斷（withdrawal）

相同劑量藥物不再產生原有效果，需加量才能達成相同效應。

questions.question: Every time the doorbell rings, Scooby howls. Now Scooby puts his tail between his legs when hearing the doorbell.
options: The doorbell is an unconditioned stimulus.
Scooby’s howling is a conditioned response.
Getting kicked is a conditioned stimulus.
The children’s rush to the door is an unconditioned response.
questions.reference_answer:
古典制約的四大要素： • 非制約刺激（unconditioned stimulus, UCS） • 非制約反應（unconditioned response, UCR） • 制約刺激（conditioned stimulus, CS） • 制約反應（conditioned response, CR）

嚎叫這個反應現在是對門鈴這個制約刺激（CS）產生的，是經由學習形成的行為，因此是制約反應（CR）。

questions.question: Partial reinforcement refers to
options: occasional, unpredictable punishment for previously reinforced responses.
learning responses that serve the function of escape from aversive stimuli.
increasing the specificity of responses required to earn a reinforcement.
the fact that behavior can be conditioned when reinforced only some of the time.
questions.reference_answer:
操作制約（operant conditioning）中的增強排程（reinforcement schedules），特別是「部分增強」（partial reinforcement）的定義

某個行為不是每次都被增強（reinforced），而是「有時候」才會獲得強化。這使得行為更抗消退（resistant to extinction），是行為維持的強力機制。 🎰 不是每次都中獎的拉霸機，反而讓人停不下來——這就是部分增強的力量。

questions.question: Flashbulb memories occur
options: due to disinhibition of childhood amnesia.
in cases of hippocampal insufficiency.
for emotionally charged significant events.
when repression is suddenly removed.
questions.reference_answer:
閃光燈記憶（flashbulb memory）

× 閃光燈記憶的特性： • 常見於重大歷史事件（例如9/11、地震、總統遇刺）或個人事件（重大情緒創傷） • 記憶內容包含：你在哪裡、誰告訴你、你當下反應是什麼 • 雖然主觀上「記得很清楚」，但研究發現，這些記憶也會隨時間扭曲或出錯 ×與之區別的概念： • 創傷記憶 （traumatic memory）：也情緒強烈，但可能會壓抑或片段化 • 程序性記憶（procedural memory）：如騎腳踏車、打字等動作技能，非此題焦點

questions.question: According to Schachter and Singer, the specific emotion we experience depends upon
options: the cause of the arousal.
environmental circumstances to which we attribute our arousal.
the particular pattern of physiological arousal.
our history of being reinforced for displaying various emotions.

這個理論徹底改變了我們對情緒的理解方式，它強調情緒不只是生理反應，而是生理喚起 + 認知解釋的交互作用。

questions.question: A test is valid if
options: it is correlated with psychologically interesting measures.
it is consistent.
the same score would be obtained if the same person took it twice.
it measures what it claims to measure.
questions.reference_answer:
心理測驗學的核心概念：效度（validity）與信度（reliability）的區別

• 信度 （reliability）：一致性（測得準不準） • 效度 （validity）：準確性（測對沒？測的是不是你說的那件事）  信度是「打靶都集中一處」，效度是「打中紅心」。兩者都要，才叫好測驗。

questions.question: In one study, dogs were exposed to an unavoidable shock. Later these dogs were unable to learn an escape response. This is an example of
options: displaced aggression.
learned helplessness.
progressive failure of adaptation.
general adaptation syndrome.
questions.reference_answer:
Martin Seligman（1975）習得無助感（Learned Helplessness）

當人覺得「無論做什麼都無效」時，就會產生逃避、退縮、自責 → 情緒低落 → 惡性循環 這導出了後來的「悲觀歸因風格」

questions.question: People are more likely to show a helpless, depressed response to negative events if their attributions are
options: external, stable, and global.
external, unstable, and global.
internal, stable, and global.
internal, unstable, and specific.
questions.reference_answer:
習得無助的歸因模型（attributional model of learned helplessness）Abramson, Seligman & Teasdale (1978)

questions.question: How do phobias differ from generalized anxiety disorders?
options: Phobias are more specific than generalized anxiety disorder.
Generalized anxiety disorder involves different biological processes than phobias.
Generalized anxiety disorder is in response to social situations; phobias can occur in response to objects or social situations.
It is easier to trace the causes of generalized anxiety disorders than phobias.
questions.reference_answer:
特定恐懼症（phobias）vs. 廣泛性焦慮症（generalized anxiety disorder, GAD）

• 恐懼症 （phobia）是對特定物體、情境、活動產生非理性且強烈的恐懼反應，如：蜘蛛、高空、飛行、社交場合。 • 廣泛性焦慮症（GAD）是一種對多重生活領域的過度、持續性擔憂與緊張，且通常無法明確指出焦慮對象。
concepts: 特定恐懼症（phobias）vs. 廣泛性焦慮症（generalized anxiety disorder, GAD）

questions.question: 負強化（negative reinforcement）是操作制約學習（operant conditioning）的其中一個類別。請回答下列兩個問題。（1）何謂負強化？（2）請舉出一個負強化現象的例子。
questions.reference_answer:
（1）負強化（negative reinforcement）是操作制約（operant conditioning）中的一種強化方式，指透過移除或減少一個不愉快的刺激（aversive stimulus）來增加某個行為在未來發生的可能性。雖然名稱中有「負」字，但結果仍然是讓行為被強化、出現頻率上升，不同於懲罰會抑制行為。

（2）例如，一位學生因為討厭每天早上被父母提醒起床，所以開始設定鬧鐘讓自己準時起床，以避免被唸（不愉快刺激）。這種「為了避免不愉快結果而增加某個行為」的情形即為負強化的表現。
concepts: 負強化
操作制約
增強

questions.question: 柯柏格（Kohlberg）以具有道德困境（moral dilemma）的故事啟動一個人道德判斷，據以決定其道德發展程度。請說明柯柏格道德發展理論的六個階段。
questions.reference_answer:
根據柯柏格（Kohlberg）的道德發展理論，人類的道德判斷能力會隨著認知成熟而發展，分為三個層級、六個階段：

【第一層級：前慣習道德階段】以避免懲罰與獲得個人利益為基礎
・第一階段「服從與懲罰導向」：判斷對錯依據是否會被懲罰
・第二階段「功利交換導向」：強調互惠原則與個人利益的交換

【第二層級：慣習道德階段】以社會角色與規範為依據
・第三階段「好孩子導向」：以取悅他人、符合期待為行為準則
・第四階段「法律與秩序導向」：強調維護法律與社會秩序

【第三層級：後慣習道德階段】以抽象原則為道德基礎
・第五階段「社會契約導向」：認為法律是人為約定，應保護基本人權，可在特殊情況下被挑戰
・第六階段「普遍倫理原則導向」：依據個人內在選擇的道德原則行動，如正義與良知，即使違背社會規範亦堅持

柯柏格主張這六階段為序進式發展，個體會依序通過，且以推理方式區辨其道德成熟度。
